verdict: OK to lend in Gurugram auto components — pursue EV-transitioning and export-linked Tier-2 suppliers with tight covenants; avoid pure ICE-engine-part makers and stressed files already in OTS.
title: Gurugram Auto & Auto Components: a note to the credit manager
narrative: Capex is lumpy — a new mould or line is ordered only after an order win, so capex should track confirmed business, not precede it. **When a proposal lands, check the buyer concentration and the receivable days first; if one OEM is above half of sales, ask for the purchase order and payment history.**

## What has changed now
**The national numbers are strong: IIP for NIC 29 output is +25.2% YoY and +19.2% Apr-to-date [D], and Haryana GST is running +10.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D].** Peer results confirm demand — Motherson Sumi Wiring profit up 35% to Rs 223 crore with revenue up 46.7% to Rs 4,054 crore [4], and Lumax lifted its growth outlook [7]. But bank credit is growing +27.0% YoY against output +19.2%, a +7.8 pp gap [D], so part of the lending is running ahead of real production. **That gap is where weak files hide; ask what the loan actually funds.**

## The local pivot and the growth pocket
**Gurgaon-Manesar MSMEs are being pushed to move from ICE parts to EV components — battery management, charging, electronics [1].** This is the growth pocket: pursue Tier-2 suppliers with a confirmed EV order, powertrain-agnostic tooling, and export enquiry. ASK Automotive's EV order wins and export push show the template [5]. **Avoid pure engine and diesel-injection part makers — rating methodology flags engine-part concentration as an obsolescence risk as EVs spread [11].** Note the local source is from September 2026 and does not quantify Gurugram's own EV adoption; collect from customer.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the receivable, not the balance sheet: invoice-discounted limits tied to confirmed OEM receivables, monthly stock-and-receivable statements, and a covenant capping debt/EBITDA.** Rating guidance flags debt/EBITDA above 2.5-2.75 times as a stress marker [10], and gross current assets of 160-170 days are normal for this trade [10] — so a file showing far more needs explanation. **Take the monthly stock statement, the receivable ageing by buyer, and GST returns every month; if ageing beyond 90 days crosses a fifth of receivables, ask for the buyer's payment confirmation.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for a buyer cutting schedules, receivables stretching past 90 days, or the unit funding a new line before the order is signed.** Gurugram already sees MSME stress in auto components and OTS activity [3], so a file that has been restructured once should not get fresh limits. **If the promoter cannot name the EV or export order behind the next capex, decline; if the order is confirmed and the buyer is a rated OEM, lend against it.**
